newsitem.title: UK: Fine Arts slumps on profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Fine Arts slumps on profit warning.

text.p: Share in Fine Art Development Plc tumbled in eary trade on Friday after the company warned results for the year to March 1997 will be "substantially below market expectations."
The stock was down 152p at 287-1/2 by 0839 GMT.

The greeting cards and mail order group said the shortfall was due mainly to a disappointing performance from its agency mail order business, where sales were some 7.5 million stg lower in the 33 weeks to November 15 than the same period last year.
Fine Arts said this represented an 11 percent decline in a period when some 75 percent of the unit's sales were made and had resulted from an unsuccessful early-season marketing campaign.
The group responded by increasing marketing expenditure by some four million stg but said this would not compensate for the low level of early season sales.
It added its greeting card wholesale operation "continues to disappoint" and a fall in sales would be "greater than expected." There had also been "some erosion in profit margins."
Fine Arts said it had taken steps to restructure the unit and had relocated the operation to one site at a cost of some one million stg.
It added that it was continuing with a disposal programme in order to focus on core activities and eliminate loss-making businesses.
